title: Restriction coherence of the constant finite perfect transition
statement:
theorem finitePerfectAdicEtaleConstant_coherence (Y : Scheme.{t})
    {A : Type t} [CommRing A] {d : AdicCoefficientDatum A}
    (T : FinitePerfectAdicAlgebraTower d) (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ {U V : Y.Etale} (f : U ⟶ V),
      (localIsomorphismRestrictionComp Y
          (ULift.{t + 1} (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1 + 1))) f).inv.app
          (finitePerfectAdicEtaleConstant Y T (n + 1)) ≫
        etaleIsomorphismNormalizationArrow Y
          (RingHom.ulift (Ideal.Quotient.factorPowSucc d.ideal (n + 1)))
          (finitePerfectAdicEtaleConstantTransition Y T n) U =
      (Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{t + 1}
          (ULift.{t + 1} (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1 + 1)))) f.left).mapDerivedCategory.map
          (etaleIsomorphismNormalizationArrow Y
            (RingHom.ulift (Ideal.Quotient.factorPowSucc d.ideal (n + 1)))
            (finitePerfectAdicEtaleConstantTransition Y T n) V) ≫
        (etaleNormalizationCoefficients f.left
          (RingHom.ulift (Ideal.Quotient.factorPowSucc d.ideal (n + 1)))).hom.app
          ((localIsomorphismRestriction Y
            (ULift.{t + 1} (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1))) V).obj
            (finitePerfectAdicEtaleConstant Y T n)) ≫
        (normalizationRestrict U.left.smallEtaleTopology
          (RingHom.ulift (Ideal.Quotient.factorPowSucc d.ideal (n + 1)))).map
          ((localIsomorphismRestrictionComp Y
            (ULift.{t + 1} (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1))) f).inv.app
            (finitePerfectAdicEtaleConstant Y T n))

proof.text: The canonical etaleNormalizationCoefficients is definitionally Functor.mapDerivedCategorySquareIso of Etale.upperStarRestrictScalarsIso. Apply the source-library theorem Etale.upperStarRestrictScalarsIso_comp_hom to the two successive inverse images, substituting the named composite U.hom using f.w.symm. Then apply Functor.mapDerivedCategorySquareIso_hom_app_comp to transport this coefficient-mate composition equation to the derived categories.

Expand each etaleIsomorphismNormalizationArrow as the image of the specified transition followed by its canonical coefficient mate. Postcompose by coefficient restriction of the hom of localIsomorphismRestrictionComp at the lower level; this is a monomorphism since it is invertible. The inverse/hom composite cancels on the right. Apply the derived coefficient-mate composition equation on the left, use naturality of the inverse of localIsomorphismRestrictionComp at the specified transition, and cancel its inverse/hom composite. This proves the original equation for every etale arrow, without using universality, finite generation, stalks, or the adic normalization hypothesis.
